system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: At each step, the system combines global memory with the current task specification to form an execution context.
system_prompt_style.note: Always-on memory layer (L1) plus task spec assembled per step.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: file_read supports segmented reads (start/count), keyword anchoring, and line-number output, so GA can inspect only the relevant regions.
env_context_strategy.note: No repo tree injected; agent explores with file/code/web tools.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: Tool outputs are first truncated with a head-tail policy to bound the size of individual messages. Redundant content in older messages is then compressed at the tag level to remove low-value fragments. When the global context budget is exceeded, the oldest messages are evicted
context_compaction.note: All three are default; compression of older messages coded as summarize.

observation_format.evidence_quote: Its browser interaction layer represents web pages through semantically structured observations rather than raw HTML
observation_format.note: Vision/screenshot capability is not a shipped default tool; unlocked by agent self-setup.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: this schema is injected into the interface, enabling GA to produce structured tool_use calls with explicit names and arguments
tool_call_format.note: README notes deprecated text-protocol sessions (ClaudeSession/LLMSession) as config-reachable alternatives.

tool_count.evidence_quote: GA exposes nine atomic tools, organized into five capability classes.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: file_patch enforces unique old_content matching and fails fast on zero or multiple matches

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: Each tool defines a name, a description, and a set of parameters described by JSON Schema, all under a consistent type function format.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: GA exposes nine atomic tools, organized into five capability classes.
protocol_standardization.note: No MCP/A2A mentioned anywhere in README or report; README contrasts Claude Code's 'Via MCP plugin' with GA's own browser control.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: The LLM processes this context and produces either direct outputs or tool calls. Tool execution is delegated to external modules, and the results are returned as structured signals that update the system state.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Working memory is continuously injected across turns, carrying only the minimal necessary task state: current objectives, constraints, and progress.
planning_granularity.note: update_working_checkpoint is a notepad rather than a structured plan object; a Plan mode exists per docs.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: GA is organized around a unified agent loop that connects the model with the environment.
multi_agent_topology.note: Conductor/Goal Hive sub-agent orchestration reachable per README roadmap.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: Conductor sub-agent orchestration. Spawn, supervise, and auto-clean parallel sub-agents; first-class delegation primitives complementing `/btw` side-questions.
delegation_mechanism.note: Default loop is single-agent; subagent_spawn reachable via Conductor/SubAgent modes.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: The Human-in-the-loop class is ask_user, used when user decisions are required.
human_in_loop.note: Model-invoked confirmation tool rather than harness gate on every action.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: update_working_checkpoint and start_long_term_update for short-term context maintenance and long-term memory distillation

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: Self-evolution pipeline compresses interaction trajectories into reusable Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), code, and skills
long_term_memory.note: L2/L3/L4 memory files under memory/ persist across sessions.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: storing historical execution sessions so the agent can reconstruct prior trajectories, audit past decisions, and recover task context when needed
state_persistence.note: TUI ships a `/continue` picker per README roadmap.

self_verification.note: Consolidation favors 'information grounded in successful execution' via reflection; no harness-run tests or linters documented.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: GA is organized around a unified agent loop that connects the model with the environment.
retry_policy.note: No task-level retry policy documented; loop simply continues.

rollback.evidence_quote: with patch tools, GA can edit text, subject to strict matching and parameter constraints; with execution and web-control tools, GA can trigger real system actions
rollback.note: No undo/revert/snapshot mechanism described in the toolset or report.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: To support long-horizon operation, GA defines explicit execution bounds that ensure controllability while preserving interruptibility and scope constraints.
termination_condition.note: Bounds not enumerated; Goal mode adds a time budget per README.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: GA therefore targets a compact budget of under 30k tokens and invests in compression rather than expansion
cost_controls.note: Mixin failover is priority-ordered, not cost-based routing.

timeouts.evidence_quote: code_run is restricted to one invocation per turn, ensuring each result is observed before the next action is planned.
timeouts.note: No tool or run timeout documented at the place where execution control is described.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: it grants any LLM system-level control over a local computer — covering browser, terminal, filesystem, keyboard/mouse input, screen vision, and mobile devices (ADB)
execution_isolation.note: code_run executes Python/PowerShell on the host; no sandbox.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: code_run, which executes Python or Bash within a controlled runtime
filesystem_access.note: Unrestricted host filesystem access within the local machine boundary.

network_policy.evidence_quote: Via code_run, GenericAgent can dynamically install Python packages, write new scripts, call external APIs, or control hardware at runtime

permission_model.evidence_quote: GA enforces a clear permission hierarchy via the injected toolset. Each tool's capability scope is strictly bounded and non-overlapping
permission_model.note: Boundaries are per-tool scope, not per-action authorisation; ask_user is model-invoked.

tracing.evidence_quote: its role is persistence and traceability, storing historical execution sessions so the agent can reconstruct prior trajectories, audit past decisions
tracing.note: L4 session archive; also `/export` in TUI.

replayability.evidence_quote: storing historical execution sessions so the agent can reconstruct prior trajectories

eval_hooks.note: Evaluation lives in a separate reproduction repo.

guardrails.evidence_quote: file_patch enforces unique old_content matching and fails fast on zero or multiple matches, reducing the risk of silent multi-location edits

target_domain.evidence_quote: it grants any LLM system-level control over a local computer — covering browser, terminal, filesystem, keyboard/mouse input, screen vision, and mobile devices (ADB)

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: The system is model-agnostic: the underlying reasoning engine (e.g., Claude, GPT, Gemini) can be replaced without affecting execution logic, tool interfaces, or memory architecture.
